headline: Bitcoin fell back below $83,000 in Asian trading as Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia pushed Brent oil above $111, even after US bitcoin ETFs took in $528M on Wednesday.

market.asOf: BTC and ETH 22 Oct 06:00 UTC (13:00 Bangkok) via CoinCodex; SOL 06:13 UTC via OKX; Fear & Greed (Alternative.me) updated 04:00 UTC via Coinbird.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips back under $83,000 as Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia push oil above $111
stories.summary: Bitcoin ran up to almost $85,000 overnight, then fell back under $83,000 in Asian trading on Thursday. Houthi attacks inside Saudi Arabia and a US order for non-emergency embassy staff to leave pushed oil higher, and a sell-off in AI stocks weighed on risky assets. Higher oil can keep inflation and interest rates up, which tends to hurt assets like crypto.
points: Bitcoin was at $82,690 on Thursday morning after reaching $84,808 overnight and dipping as low as $82,567, per CryptoTicker (06:24 UTC; live prices are at the top of the page).
The total crypto market value was $2.785 trillion, down 2.64% over 24 hours, per the same report.
At 06:26 GMT Brent oil was up $2.82, or 2.59%, at $111.64 a barrel, and US crude (WTI) was up $2.24 at $99.39, per Reuters data.
The State Department ordered non-emergency embassy staff and their families to leave "in Saudi Arabia only". One person was killed and 8 wounded at Dammam airport, per ABC News.
Investing.com blamed "a deep selldown in artificial intelligence stocks and a continued rise in oil prices" for the drop.

stories.title: US bitcoin ETFs take in $528M in a day, but the price still slips
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors, took in a net $528 million on Wednesday 21 Oct, led by BlackRock and Fidelity. Ether, Solana and XRP funds also had small inflows. The money coming in has not been enough to stop Thursday's price drop.
points: Bitcoin ETFs had a net inflow of $528.41M on 21 Oct, taking October to +$463.3M so far, per Trader T data reported by KuCoin.
By fund: BlackRock's IBIT +$235M, Fidelity's FBTC +$212.71M, Grayscale's GBTC +$32.59M, Bitwise's BITB +$19.23M (same source).
Ether ETFs took in $14.96M, XRP funds $708,520 and Solana funds $585,300, per Gokhshtein.
Inflows are about $1.1B so far this week after $909.6M of outflows over the two weeks before, citing SoSoValue, per Traders Union.

stories.title: The OCC finalizes a GENIUS Act stablecoin rule, and banks push back
stories.summary: The OCC, a federal bank regulator, issued a final rule under the GENIUS Act stablecoin law. It drops a proposed limit on stablecoin rewards arranged through third parties. The American Bankers Association accuses the OCC of undermining what Congress intended.
points: The final rule drops a proposed presumption against stablecoin yield arranged through third parties, per The Block.
ABA CEO Rob Nichols said "attempting to address deposit flight and economic harm after it has occurred is the wrong approach."
The ABA warned the rule risks "threatening the funds banks use to make the loans that drive the U.S. economy," per The Block.
The rule takes effect on 18 Jan 2027, per KuCoin's daily market report.

briefs.title: Tesla books a $288M paper gain on its bitcoin
briefs.summary: Tesla's Q3 gain on its bitcoin is unrealized: its digital assets rose in value from $674M to $962M. Independent board committees at SpaceX and Tesla are studying a merger, but no terms are agreed.

briefs.title: Bitcoin volatility near its 2026 low
briefs.summary: Bitcoin's 28-day realized volatility is 1.2%, near this year's low, ahead of the 28 Oct Fed decision and the 3 Nov US midterms, per The Block citing K33.

briefs.title: Short sellers squeezed in Wednesday's rally
briefs.summary: CoinGlass counted $267.49M of liquidations in 24 hours as of Wednesday evening, $208.49M (78.3%) of them bets on a fall.

briefs.title: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade goes live
briefs.summary: The upgrade cuts the time for a Solana transaction to become final from about 12.8 seconds to about 150 milliseconds.

briefs.title: Grayscale lets investors pay in crypto for 10 funds
briefs.summary: Investors can now contribute tokens instead of cash to 10 Grayscale products, including its BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP funds.

briefs.title: Comments close on the SEC's crypto offering proposal
briefs.summary: Comments on the SEC's proposed crypto offering rule were due 20 Oct. It would create a $5M startup exemption plus $20M and $75M tiers. It is still only a proposal.
